summary: The milestone completed 12 experiments in 244.5 minutes, with 6 compute-bound. The longest recorded compute-bound task was 55.28 minutes; the locked task-conditioned indicator reports no GPU-idle condition during compute-bound work.
bottlenecks_identified: The compute-bound transition, evidence-preservation, and allocation task formed the largest recorded long tail at 55.28 minutes, but the supplied timing receipt has no phase breakdown, so its runtime cause cannot be assigned.

The parity-tested batched SamplerBack synthesis task was second-longest overall at 45.63 minutes; its synthesis-only classification makes GPU inactivity expected, and the supplied evidence does not show whether profiling, coding, parity testing, or artifact finalization dominated.

Three other compute-bound entries in the supplied slowest-five list took 24.7, 23.1, and 22.72 minutes; their labels identify gated proposal-stream, continuous-learning, and GGUF-family work, but the aggregate durations do not separate setup, model loading, compute, verification, or artifact finalization.
Per-task accelerator efficiency cannot be quantified because the GPU snapshot is not correlated with experiment intervals; the locked idle-on-compute indicator is false.
No supplied evidence identifies a compute-bound task that loaded 2+ models in parallel, so no DualGPURunner selection failure can be established.
improvements_suggested: Emit monotonic per-phase timings for setup, gate waiting, model loading, compute, verification, and artifact finalization in every experiment receipt.
Attach task-scoped GPU telemetry to compute-bound receipts, including the sampling window, device utilization, process-to-model mapping, and selected runner.
Declare expected model concurrency before launch and select DualGPURunner only when 2+ models are actually loaded in parallel; keep single-model jobs on one GPU.
Cache and incrementally assemble terminal evidence, retirement state, and milestone allocation inputs, then use phase receipts to verify whether this shortens the 55.28-minute transition path.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument every experiment with phase-level timing receipts so the next long task has an attributable cause.
Add incremental, cached assembly for transition evidence and allocation inputs, targeting the longest recorded compute-bound workflow.
Correlate GPU telemetry and model concurrency with each compute task, automatically choosing DualGPURunner only for declared parallel multi-model work.
meta_reflection: This retrospective can rank the slow paths but cannot explain them because milestone evidence aggregates each experiment into one duration and provides only a terminal GPU snapshot. Task-correlated phase and accelerator receipts are prerequisites for a defensible nonzero savings estimate next milestone.
